::: notes
The last session used your IDE as a place to type. This one is about the IDE itself, and it names Positron throughout, because Positron is the IDE of the course and the one on my screen. If you work in RStudio or VS Code, stay there: every step has its counterpart, and one slide in the last section says where each thing sits. There are four sections. First the folder and the window: how the workspace opens and what each part of the window is for. Then running code, from a whole script to a part of one statement, and the objects that the session holds once the code has run. Then the places where you look at things, the data, the plots and the help pages. And last the terminal, the other IDEs, and what to do when the window misbehaves.
:::
